column1: # `scripts/audit-name-derived-offsets.py` counts hand-written offset constants and asks where
# each one's value came from. Its headline number is only useful if it counts the RIGHT rows:
# a census that lumps `DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH = 1` and a Windows `CONTEXT` register slot in with
# `CS::CSSystemStep + 0x48` reports a number nobody can act on.
# So every row that is NOT an unprovenanced ELDEN RING object-field offset has to say so HERE,
# with a reason, in a file a reviewer can read. Rows absent from this table are classified by
# the name-shape rule in the audit script; this table overrides that rule in both directions --
# it can pull a row OUT of the game bucket and it can force one IN that the name shape misses.
# The point of writing it down rather than widening a regex: a regex that quietly drops rows
# makes the census smaller without making it truer, and nobody can tell afterwards which rows
# went. Every exclusion below is one line someone can disagree with.
#   OS-ABI        A structure defined by Windows, the MSVC ABI, or a PE/COFF file -- not by
#                 FromSoftware. It cannot be measured against the ELDEN RING images, and it does
#                 not drift when the game patches. `--selftest` checks each of these against the
#                 published layout, so they are VERIFIED rather than merely excused.
#   MACHINE-CODE  A byte offset INSIDE an x86-64 instruction encoding or a patch site. Wrong
#                 values here corrupt a write, but the witness is the instruction encoding, not
#   OUR-OWN       An offset into a structure or buffer this workspace defines. There is no game
#                 object to measure it against; the definition is the truth.
#   FORMAT        An offset into a file this workspace parses (save container, `.gfx`, param
#                 row, SPIR-V). A wrong value fails a parse or reads our own `Vec`; it does not
#                 silently return a neighbouring field of a live game object.
#   NOT-AN-OFFSET Not an offset at all -- an enum value, a count, a limit, a state code.
#   GAME          An ELDEN RING layout constant the name-shape rule does not recognise. Forced
# Every name here must still match at least one live definition; `--selftest` fails if one
# stops existing, so the table cannot rot into a list of ghosts.
# ---- Windows x64 CONTEXT (winnt.h). P1-P6Home 0x00..0x28, ContextFlags 0x30, MxCsr 0x34, the
# ---- six segment words 0x38..0x42, EFlags 0x44, Dr0-Dr3 0x48..0x60, Dr6 0x68, Dr7 0x70, then
# ---- the integer file Rax 0x78, Rcx 0x80, Rdx 0x88, Rbx 0x90, Rsp 0x98, Rbp 0xa0, Rsi 0xa8,
# ---- PE/COFF. e_lfanew 0x3c; from the PE signature: Machine +0x4, NumberOfSections +0x6,
# ---- Name[8] 0x0, VirtualSize 0x8, VirtualAddress 0xc. DataDirectory sits at +96 in
# ---- IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER32 (it is +112 in the PE32+ form, which is why the name says PE32).
# ---- MSVC ABI. These live inside the game's memory but the layout is the compiler's, not
# ---- FromSoftware's, so a 1.16.2-vs-1.17 drift check has nothing to say about them.
# ---- DEVMODEW (wingdi.h), the Unicode form: dmDeviceName[32] WCHAR 0x00..0x40, dmSpecVersion
# ---- 0x40, dmDriverVersion 0x42, dmSize 0x44, dmDriverExtra 0x46, dmFields 0x48, the position/
# ---- 0x66..0xa6, dmLogPixels 0xa6, dmBitsPerPel 0xa8, then the two below.
# ---- Byte offsets inside an instruction encoding, not inside an object.
